title: Open a child-locked cupboard, key held over the latch
instruction: Open the cupboard door wide and put the key back on its spot.
context: Why: magnetic cabinet locks are the usual child-proofing fit for the low kitchen and bathroom cupboards that hold cleaning products and medicines: the latch is screwed inside the door, invisible from outside, and only a magnetic key held against the door's face pulls it free. The maker's guide (Safety 1st Magnetic Locking System) says: place the magnetic key over the area where the lock is installed, hear the click as the lock disengages, open the door; closing the door re-engages it. The latch is sprung: take the key away before pulling and it drops straight back onto its catch, so one hand keeps the key flat on the door over the latch, riding with the door, while the other pulls the knob until the latch's hook has cleared the catch; only then can the key come away. Done by: parents and carers in homes with small children, several times a day.
setup: Cupboard: a white melamine low storage cabinet on the table straight ahead of the robot, front toward it: a carcass of 16 mm chipboard panels 330 mm wide, 300 mm deep and 340 mm tall, its front edge 37.5 cm ahead of the arm bases and spanning from 27 cm right to 6 cm left of their midline, held to the table (30 kg in the sim, standing in for its screws). One door of 18 mm MDF, 320 mm wide and 320 mm tall (1.4 kg), overlays the open front on a vertical hinge at its right edge (opens to 110 deg; hinge friction 0.05 N m, so it stays where it is left). A 30 mm round zinc knob, 25 mm proud, sits 35 mm in from the door's free (left) edge, 15 cm up. Lock: a Safety 1st magnetic child lock screwed inside the door, 30 mm in from its free edge and 30 cm up, its plastic catch under the cabinet top; the parents' 20 mm yellow sticker on the door's outer face marks the lock's centre. The lock is set: the door opens 1 mm of play and stops. Key: the Safety 1st magnetic key, a green ABS plastic puck 40 mm across and 14 mm thick with a magnet inside, 25 g, lying flat on its spot, a 60 mm grey circle on the table 30 cm ahead and 20 cm left of the midline. How the lock works: the latch is pulled free while the key's centre is within 12 mm of the lock's centre on the door face, the key's face within 5 mm of the door and tilted under 15 deg; away from there it springs back. Its hook needs 6 mm of door travel at the lock to clear the catch; until then, if the key leaves, it drops back and holds the door where it is. Both arms start at their ready poses. One fixed layout, matching the screenshot.
scoring: Read at the end of the run from the sim state (in a real trial: a protractor taped at the hinge, a steel rule against the door's corner, top and side photos, and the video). 0: anything else, including the untouched start, or the cabinet pushed more than 5 mm off its marks at any time. 0.25: the door not past the catch (under 3 deg open) but the key flat over the lock at the end (within the release rule above). 0.5: the door opened past the catch (3 deg or more) but under 45 deg. 0.75: the door open 45 deg or more, but the key not lying flat (under 10 deg) inside its 60 mm circle, or a gripper within 40 mm of the door, its knob or the key, or any of them moving more than 1 mm over the last 1 s. 1.0: the door open 45 deg or more (its free edge then stands 245 mm from where it closes, room to reach in and lift out a bottle of cleaner), the key lying flat inside its circle, both grippers at least 40 mm clear of the door, knob and key, and nothing moving more than 1 mm over the last 1 s.
reset_notes: Close the door until the latch clicks onto its catch and check it holds against a pull; set the key flat on its circle; check the cabinet is on its taped outline. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at real size; the round key and knob are discs of 8 boxes. The magnet is a declared rule, not a field: the latch is free while the key's centre is within 12 mm of the lock, its face within 5 mm of the door and tilted under 15 deg; until the door has moved 6 mm at the lock the hook drops back the moment the key leaves. The key is taken not to cling (checked before trials). The arms reach about 55 deg of the door's arc. Hinge friction 0.05 N m, static equal to dynamic.
